environment.transport: loopback HTTP; app→PG on isolated Docker bridge; no external network/proxy/TLS

methodology.order: Photo and shift queries alternate within each repetition; their leading order alternates. Baseline phase precedes indexed phase.
methodology.sql: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON); planner Execution Time excludes HTTP/auth/ORM overhead, and client wall time includes the local round trip.
methodology.parameters: Last20 OperationEntry IDs at the start of the experiment; fixed userId=1 for personal shift history.
caveats: Small synthetic fixture, warm shared buffers and OS cache; no cold-cache claims.
Index creation itself warms pages, so before/after phases are not a fully randomized crossover.
Only30 observations per query/phase: medians describe this run and are not a capacity or p95 production estimate.
The direct SQL probes approximate two route/relation query shapes; they do not measure end-to-end API improvements.
Indexes add write, storage and migration costs, which this experiment does not benchmark.
SELECT of photo IDs does not read or transmit stored photo bytes.

1cpu.reason: Export was repeated in a fresh1CPU process with all three requests inside the timed and SQL-statistics window. The initial export timing wrapper was superseded; other cases are unchanged.

0.1cpu.reason: The initial phase began while the0.1CPU container was still starting and saw12 immediate ECONNRESETs. Warm comparison was repeated after explicit HTTP readiness,30 successful warm-up requests and a fresh identical fixture. Initial cold/preparation observations are preserved separately and not counted as warm-service failures.
